status: Merged diagnostic cycle, forced rebuilt and full-output verified. No production scheduling change or speedup claim.
methodology: Instrumented root-stage and task-span evidence. Phase wall intervals are disjoint within a root; root summaries, planner setup and final structure/distribution are outside these phase totals but remain inside complete-region measurement. Process CPU includes service/shader threads and observer work; phase CPU/wall is not an available-core utilization percentage. Worker occupancy means a task is in flight, including nested work, blocking and preemption; one physical thread is counted once. Only complete ready-state cases should inform CPU interpretation. Do not turn call/stack/task counts into elapsed-time shares or claim ordinary speedups.

finding: Joined anchor evaluation dominates observed root phases. Standard seeds spend a weighted 35.62% and 37.59% of evaluation with at most two physical workers carrying a top-level task. Brown mushroom and large ancient debris longest tasks lie outside the requested region in all 20 regions per standard seed. Those long tasks usually begin early; simple queue reordering alone is not supported as a sufficient fix. Basalt pillars instead carry about 13.6 tasks in flight while process CPU/wall is about 0.8; that pattern is consistent with waits but does not distinguish GPU, dependency, OS or observer effects.

next_opportunity.candidate: Reduce exact exterior dependency critical paths and demand-driven GPU waits. Reuse source ordering and complete closure; do not truncate the boundary or simply enlarge thread counts. Inspect held frontier/graph/checkpoint experiments before selecting a distinct design.
next_opportunity.uncertainty: This evidence identifies phase and task-span patterns, not the causal share of GPU, dependency wait or preemption. Long tasks commonly start early, so priority-only scheduling may offer limited benefit. Earlier broad frontiers and graph replay had tradeoffs; no revival is justified solely by occupancy.

limitations: Known external host activity is recorded; no uncontended performance, no-regression or subsecond acceptance.
Observer timings include event collection and summary overhead and are not ordinary measurements. Summary time remains inside the complete region interval.
CPU/wall is process CPU time, not fraction of available cores. Workers with a task in flight may be blocked, preempted or executing nested work.
Root phase totals exclude setup, observer summaries and final structure/distribution/retirement; whole region includes them.
Ordinary library bytes differ from C58 despite no production algorithm/layout change; separate full-NBT validation is retained.
No concurrency/portal lifecycle rerun selected for this diagnostic-only cycle. These requirements remain open for final acceptance.
